summary: The system is experiencing multiple concurrent issues: (1) the external payment service provider (PSP) is returning 503 Service Unavailable, causing payment failures; (2) the inventory-db connection pool is exhausted because connections are held for over 6 seconds; and (3) the orders service has crashed repeatedly due to being OOMKilled under load.

alerts.name: PodCrashLooping
alerts.summary: orders: container restarted 2.034 times in 10 minutes

hypotheses.summary: The external payment service provider (PSP) is returning 503 Service Unavailable, causing the payments service to fail charge transactions and propagate 502 Bad Gateway errors back to orders.

evidence.shows: The payment service is failing because of 503 Service Unavailable errors returned by the external PSP.
Outbound requests from payments to the psp have a 63% failure rate, which was 0% previously.

hypotheses.suggested_fix: Contact the external Payment Service Provider (PSP) support team regarding their 503 Service Unavailable errors, or configure the payments service to fall back to an alternate payment provider.

hypotheses.summary: The inventory-db connection pool is exhausted due to database connections being held too long (up to 6s), causing request timeouts and failures across various endpoints.

evidence.quote: SQLTransientConnectionException: inventory-db - Connection is not available, request timed out after 2000ms
evidence.shows: The inventory service is unable to obtain database connections, causing request threads to wait and time out.
Connections in the inventory-db pool are being held for up to 6.075 seconds, which exceeds the Hikari connection timeout of 2 seconds.

hypotheses.suggested_fix: Investigate and optimize slow database queries or check for transaction lock contention in Postgres on the inventory-db, and consider enlarging the database connection pool configuration.

hypotheses.summary: The orders service experienced container crashes due to being OOMKilled, likely caused by memory saturation under load or a JVM-level memory leak.

evidence.quote: restarted 3.01 times in window (last termination: OOMKilled)
evidence.shows: The orders container has crashed multiple times in the window due to running out of memory (OOMKilled).

evidence.quote: Back-off restarting failed container orders in pod
evidence.shows: The orders pod is experiencing container restarts and back-offs due to crashes.

hypotheses.suggested_fix: Capture and analyze heap dumps from the orders service to detect memory leaks, and temporarily increase memory limits for the orders container.
